hypotheses.text: In the seminal cohort of 20 individuals with monoallelic DHX9 variants reported by Calame et al. (2023), the denominator of individuals exhibiting neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) phenotypes rather than isolated peripheral neuropathy (CMT2) is strictly less than 20/20 due to phenotypic bifurcation across variant domains.
hypotheses.rationale: Calame et al. identified 20 individuals with de novo/rare DHX9 variants whose phenotypic spectrum ranged from NDDs to the distal symmetric polyneuropathy Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2 (CMT2). Establishing the exact fraction presenting with core ID/DD versus isolated axonal neuropathy is essential to prevent conflating CMT2 cases into the intellectual disability phenotype denominator.

evidence.text: Using exome sequencing and family-based rare-variant analyses, we identified 20 individuals with de novo, ultra-rare, heterozygous missense or loss-of-function (LoF) DHX9 variant alleles. Phenotypes ranged from NDDs to the distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2).

hypotheses.text: Structural cardiac malformations (such as ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy or conduction defects) represent an ultra-rare finding in DHX9-related neurodevelopmental disorder occurring in fewer than 10% of reported patients, rather than a recurrent core manifestation.
hypotheses.rationale: Yamada et al. (2023) described a patient with a heterozygous de novo DHX9 p.(Gly414Arg) variant who had intellectual disability, short stature, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy, along with cardiac conduction abnormalities in mutant mice. Determining whether cardiac anomalies occur across the Calame cohort or remain isolated to specific ATP-binding domain mutations clarifies whether cardiac screening is warranted in all newly diagnosed DHX9 patients.

evidence.text: Herein, we report a patients with a heterozygous de novo missense variant, p.(Gly414Arg) of DHX9 who presented with a short stature, intellectual disability, and ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy... heterozygous mice showed a reduced body size, reduced emotionality, and cardiac conduction abnormality.

hypotheses.text: Epileptic seizures occur in less than 30% of individuals in the DHX9 NDD cohort, making epilepsy a supportive but non-obligate feature that distinguishes DHX9-related NDD from highly epileptogenic DEAH-box/DEAD-box paralogous disorders.
hypotheses.rationale: Calame et al. (2023) and general paralog reviews highlight clinical features such as developmental delay and epilepsy, but quantitative assessment is needed to distinguish whether seizures are an infrequent complication or a core diagnostic hallmark of DHX9 disruption compared to other DExH/D-box helicase disorders (e.g., DHX30 or DDX3X).

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient numerators and denominators for brain MRI findings, speech delay, seizures, and dysmorphic features in Table 1 or Supplementary Table S1 of Calame et al. (2023)?
new_directions.rationale: Directly parsing the primary tables of the seminal Calame et al. (AJHG 2023) paper will provide authoritative, un-aggregated ratios for each individual HPO feature across all 20 individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of DHX9 variants in published cohorts are loss-of-function versus missense, and what are the exact phenotype frequencies within each of these two molecular subgroups?
new_directions.rationale: Calame et al. identified clear HPO-based segregation between mild NDD in LoF cases and severe NDD in nuclear localization signal (NLS) missense cases; separating numerators by variant mechanism will resolve whether phenotype frequencies should be reported separately.
